blind.why: 5 m in Hub (dist_5 vs t2_007). The CS2 soldier stands in a grounded, weighty rifle-ready stance with a clean figure-ground read. Ours has thin, gangly limbs. The Ember teammate (tan/cream/orange) melts into the tan sandstone wall, and the Tide figure reads as a glowing hologram, not a solid athlete.

15 m toward Mid Doors (dist_15 vs t1_010). The Tide figures pop well, and that is better than CS2. But the Ember teammate beside them is camouflaged by the fruit stall and the warm walls. The CS2 players are solid, bulky and readable. Ours are spindly stick figures.

Moving bot at mid range (run_1 vs ss_18). Our run cycle has a real stride, but the checkerboard and gingham suit patterns are visually noisy. The far Ember bots read as purple/maroon with violet helmets and wings. CS2's firing pose has weight and a muzzle read.

biggest_gap: The team lock covers only the suit hue, so Ember still camouflages on the sand map and secondary colours carry the wrong team. Repro: ?test=1&seed=7&match=1&phase=live, advance(8), then dump ctx.characters.model(a).u. Tide #6 helmet accent is #ff5a3c (Ember orange-red) with a #663cdd purple jetpack. Tide #7 has an indigo helmet (#5e61ba), violet accent and a purple pattern. Tide #10 has hot-pink helmet accent and back (#ff7ac8/#dd3c9a). Ember #2 has a periwinkle accent (#9499db). The Ember suits (#973621 to #db4624) and cream accents (#e9d8bd) sit at the same luminance as the sandstone and terracotta. In seed 3 at 15 m (dist_15) the Ember figure vanishes into the fruit stall and walls, while Tide pops. In seed 5 (run_0) the Ember bots read as maroon/purple with violet helmets. CS2 keeps each side to one value and silhouette family that contrasts with the map. Fix: clamp ALL slots (helmet, helmet accent, back, pattern colour, accent) to a team band or neutral grey, and never allow the opposite team's hue. Give Ember a darker value base (umber or charcoal) with saturated orange bands, so it holds at least 3:1 luminance contrast against the sandstone.
other_gaps: Silhouette is spindly. Limbs are 2 to 3 px wide at 30 m, and the narrow torso reads as a stick mannequin next to CS2's bulky geared bodies. Thicken the forearms, shins and torso, and add mass at the hips and shoulders.
High-contrast suit patterns (checker, gingham and stripes, patN 1/3/5/6/7) break up the body like camouflage at 15 to 30 m. Cap the pattern contrast or fade it out with distance.

Reload (Q_reload_0.9/1.4): the off hand is flung out sideways with an open palm and no visible magazine. Throw at 0.25 s is just the gun hand swinging down, with no overhead wind-up and nothing in the hand.
Spawn materialise keeps Tide models as a glowing translucent hologram about 1 s into the live phase (dist_5), so they read as ghosts at the moment they first matter.
Draw calls: 9 actors in view add 52 calls and 62k tris (about 5.8 calls and 6.9k tris per actor including shadows), above the claimed 4.8.
The head capsule is about 0.33 to 0.35 m wide (crown r=0.165), which is generous next to CS2's tight head box. Make sure it matches the helmet mesh and not empty air.
bugs: The hitbox debug overlay stays drawn on a tagged, frozen actor until the shatter, because update() continues on m.tag before hbDbg.visible is cleared (index.js:124 vs 130). Debug only.
strengths: Tide reads instantly at 15 to 30 m on the warm map. Tag-out goes from a clean ice freeze to a confetti shatter, with no bloom-disc bug. Tagged actors are excluded from hit tests. Hitboxes now give the head priority and the crown starts at about 1.5 m. The run cycle has real stride and knee bend. Crouch is compact and keeps team colour. The reload now tilts the gun. There were no console errors.
